lang.name: English
start.greeting:
Hello! I am NetSentinel — your network security monitoring assistant.
Know what changed, and what deserves your attention.
help.title: All commands
auth.denied:
⛔ Not recognised. Access is limited to authorised users.
If you are the operator, add your numeric user ID to ALLOWED_USER_IDS and restart the bot.
auth.disabled: ⛔ Your account has been disabled. Please contact the operator.
scan.started:
🔍 Scan Started
Target: {target} ({value})
Profile: {profile}
Status: Running…
scheduled.no_operator: ⚠️ No operator chat recorded; the scheduled alert was not sent.
target.name_bad_chars: Target name contains unsupported characters: {chars}. Use letters, digits, dash, underscore or dot.
target.name_dot_edge: Target name may not start or end with a dot.
target.list_empty:
No targets registered.
Add one with: /addtarget <name> <value>
purge.usage:
Usage: /purge <name> confirm
⚠️ This deletes the target and ALL of its scan history.
purge.confirm_prompt:
⚠️ This will permanently delete target '{name}' ({value}) and its history:
  • {scans} scan(s)
  • {hosts} host(s)
  • {services} service(s)
  • {changes} change event(s)
  • {schedules} schedule(s)

To proceed: {command}
purge.done:
🗑 Purged '{name}':
  • {scans} scan(s)
  • {hosts} host(s)
  • {services} service(s)
  • {changes} change event(s)
  • {schedules} schedule(s)
  • 1 target
schedule.usage:
⏱ Scheduled monitoring
/schedule list — show all schedules
/schedule add <target> <profile> <hours>
/schedule remove <target>
/schedule pause <target>
/schedule resume <target>
/schedule pause-all
/schedule resume-all
schedule.disabled_suffix: ⚠️ Scheduler is disabled (SCHEDULE_ENABLED=false); the schedule is saved but will not fire.
schedule.bad_interval: ❌ Interval must be a whole number of hours, got '{value}'.
schedule.min_interval: ❌ Interval must be at least 1 hour.
schedule.no_schedule: ❌ No schedule for '{name}'. Use /schedule add to create one.
schedule.list_empty:
No schedules configured.
Add one with: /schedule add <target> <profile> <hours>
history.usage: Usage: /scans <target> — show history for a target
